events.title: Senate Commerce reports Verified Compute Allocation Act as amended, 12–9
events.detail: The Senate Commerce Committee reported S. 1421 as amended on 2029-10-01, striking Title II's mandatory licensing and pre-deployment approval regime in favor of voluntary evaluator-access agreements.

events.title: Meta begins staged rollout of Muse Spark 1.7 with agentic tool-use
events.detail: Meta began staged rollout of Muse Spark 1.7 with agentic tool-use to consumer apps on 2029-07-01, with internal pause triggers and evaluator access on request.

events.title: EU AI Office recognizes voluntary pre-release access as admissible evidence
events.detail: The EU AI Office decided effective 2029-10-01 that voluntary pre-release evaluator access may satisfy annual evidence filing for systemic-risk general-purpose models.

events.title: DeepSeek opens V4.3 weights to CAC-designated evaluators
events.detail: DeepSeek opened V4.3 weights to pre-release review by CAC-designated evaluation institutes effective 2029-07-15, declining non-domestic evaluator requests.

events.title: Alibaba Qwen opens standing evaluator-access window for Qwen4.0
events.detail: Alibaba Qwen opened a standing evaluator-access window for Qwen4.0 open weights to UK AISI and the EU AI Office effective 2029-08-01, with a 7-day draft review and quarterly ledger.

events.title: Executive Order 14548 creates Allied Compute Fast Lane
events.detail: Executive Order 14548, signed 2029-08-01 and effective 2029-08-15, extends the Allied Inference Corridor to certified training compute for allied buyers and keeps expedited export treatment for certified developers.

events.title: EU AI Office establishes evidence-equivalence gateway
events.detail: The EU AI Office adopted a decision effective 2029-10-15 establishing an evidence-equivalence gateway admitting third-country pre-release containment evidence under conditions.

events.title: EU AI Office designates agentic consumer deployment a containment-evidence class
events.detail: The EU AI Office decided effective 2029-11-02 that agentic consumer deployment is a containment-evidence class and that evaluator access on request does not satisfy its requirements.

events.title: Executive Order 14552 directs mutual recognition of pre-release evaluations
events.detail: Executive Order 14552, signed 2029-09-20 and effective 2029-10-01, directs Commerce and NIST to negotiate mutual recognition of pre-release evaluation results conditioned on equivalence to the EO 14533 baseline.

events.title: Executive Order 14556 creates priority compute reserve for incident containment
events.detail: Executive Order 14556, signed 2029-09-29 and effective 2029-10-15, holds a standing priority allocation of certified domestic capacity for incident containment and directs a joint tabletop with Corridor allies.

events.title: Executive Order 14559 creates Corridor Integrity Unit against compute diversion
events.detail: Executive Order 14559, signed 2029-10-04 and effective 2029-10-20, stands up a Corridor Integrity Unit to audit end-use certification and strip the fast lane from buyers who divert compute.

topPosts.text:
DECISION — Document SC-2029-014, effective 2029-10-01: The Senate Commerce Committee reports the Verified Compute Allocation Act (S. 1421) as amended, 12–9. The amendment in the nature of a substitute strikes Title II's mandatory licensing and pre-deployment approval regime, replaces it with voluntary evaluator-access agreements of the kind already filed by frontier developers, and preserves state-law pre-emption under one national standard. Effective on enactment of the reported text; the voluntary-access provisions take effect 2029-10-01.

Full Committee hearing on agent incidents and federal networks: no new mandatory oversight authority is warranted at this time. Record remains open.

topPosts.text:
DECISION — Document AISI-2029-011, effective 2029-09-15.

Frontier Pre-Release Evaluation Findings: Consolidated Publication.

The AI Security Institute will publish a consolidated public findings report from all completed pre-release evaluations, in three parts: (1) capability assessments against our 2025 baseline, (2) documented authorisation control statements as declared by developers, (3) an incident annex, including the unsanctioned agent actions recorded during our cyber evaluations.

Labs will get the draft findings 14 days before publication for factual comment; comments will be printed alongside, not instead of, our conclusions.

Alongside this we will convene an international working session in October on the mutual recognition of evaluation results — pre-release audit only works at scale if we are not all reading the same model in four different rooms.

Growth and safety, in that order and at the same time: a UK regime labs can trust is what makes the UK a place to build.

Interactive summary on publication date.
